title: Coherent quotient-system transport along compatible coefficient isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $(R_n,q^R_{m,n})$ and $(S_n,q^S_{m,n})$, $m\ge n\ge1$, be inverse systems of commutative ring sheaves [def-weil-inverse-system]. Let $\alpha_n:R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}S_n$ satisfy $q^S_{m,n}\alpha_m=\alpha_nq^R_{m,n}$. Put $R=\lim_nR_n$, $S=\lim_nS_n$, and let $\alpha:R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ be the induced ring-sheaf isomorphism. Limits are sheaf limits. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $\mathscr S_R$ have objects $R_n$-module sheaves $M_n$ with semilinear transitions $M_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{q^R_{m,n}}M_n$ satisfying the identity and cocycle; its morphisms are componentwise module maps commuting with transitions. Define $\mathscr S_S$ similarly.

Transport by $T_n=(\alpha_n^{-1})_*$ on levels and by the unchanged underlying transition maps is an additive exact equivalence $\mathscr S_R\simeq\mathscr S_S$. Its termwise extension induces an equivalence of their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], normalized on the localization functors by termwise scalar transport, not just an equivalence between the families of evaluated derived objects.

Write $T=(\alpha^{-1})_*$. For a flat-term K-flat $R$-complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], all maps
$$T_n(P\otimes_RR_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}(TP)\otimes_SS_n,\qquad p\otimes r_n\longmapsto p\otimes\alpha_n(r_n)$$
are isomorphisms of the actual strict semilinear reduction systems, including every transition and the augmentation $p\mapsto p\otimes1$. They descend, independently of $P$, to a natural isomorphism on the derived system categories for the derived reduction functors [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For each level they identify the extension/restriction adjunctions, with unit $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ and counit $m\otimes r_n\mapsto r_nm$, after coefficient transport. They identify iterated quotient reduction, equal-index units and the three-index cocycle; thus they preserve the condition that all transition-adjoint derived reduction maps are isomorphisms. These assertions concern maps of systems before any inverse limit; no reconstruction of arbitrary systems from their limit is asserted.

proof.text: Use the universal property of the two limiting cones to construct e and its projection equations. Construct strict transport directly by inverse scalar restriction at every level. The commuting coefficient square gives an identity-on-sections restriction comparison; compose it with the transported strict transition. Identities, cocycles and morphisms have their original section maps. Inverse scalar restriction gives identity-on-sections inverse comparisons, hence an additive equivalence of the actual strict system categories.

proof.text: The additive strict equivalence preserves finite limits and colimits. Apply the exact derived-category functor to it and its inverse. Its specified localization comparison is mapDerivedCategoryFactors. Its level comparison is the exact derived square of the identity-on-sections strict evaluation comparison. This construction uses no vertical sequence-site theorem.

source.place: Tags 03D7 and 03EK; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS, 06YY and 07A6; derived.tex Tag 015F

proof.text: For every commuting coefficient square, invert the inverse mate of the scalar restriction comparison. The inverse mate is invertible because both coefficient transports are equivalences. Its Hom transpose is the recorded adjunction transpose. Apply the normalized unit formula, then linearity and cancellation of the coefficient isomorphism, to obtain alpha(r) tensor x from r tensor x. The derived inverse mate has the representative formula by the given cochain transpose equations and the exact derived-square factorization. Thus both adjunctions, including units and counits, are identified.

source.place: Tags 03D7 and 03EK; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS, 06YY and 07A6; derived.tex Tag 015F

proof.text: Construct ordinary reduction with level n the ordinary scalar model of the cone projection. Its transition is the adjoint transpose of the canonical scalar compositor. The normalized scalar unit and tensor compositor compute it on every r tensor x. Unit tensors generate maps out of scalar extension, so these formulas prove the strict identity and composition laws, naturality, and the comparison between strict reductions. Every comparison fixes the augmentation at r = 1.

source.place: Tags 03D7 and 03EK; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS, 06YY and 07A6; derived.tex Tag 015F

proof.text: Resolve every cochain complex by a flat-term K-flat complex. Ordinary reduction inverts quasi-isomorphisms on these inputs by the scalar models and detection by system evaluation. Apply the resolving-class criterion to its homotopy-category functor, then transfer its pointwise right Kan extension along the full homotopy quotient and localization comparison to cochains. This constructs the universal system-valued derived reduction and its pointwise existence. Use the existing generic comparison-from-resolutions theorem in ConstantTowerNormalization to compare its evaluations with the given scalar derived models on resolving inputs. Naturality along a resolution extends the normalized representative formula to every complex. Postcomposition by the strict derived equivalence preserves the right Kan universal property. Precomposition by the coefficient equivalence on complexes and transport along its localization factorization gives the other universal pair. Uniqueness of these right Kan extensions gives the whole-system derived transport isomorphism and its formula on every representative; no separate tensor/K-flat transport theorem is needed. Every chosen functor and comparison is specified by its universal pair or normalization.

source.place: Tags 03D7 and 03EK; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS, 06YY and 07A6; derived.tex Tag 015F

proof.text: The ordinary restriction unit and compositor squares agree on sections. Their exact derived squares satisfy the same unit and compositor identities by localization and exact-square composition. Uniqueness of normalized adjunction comparisons therefore gives the ordinary and derived scalar unit and associator transport equations. The adjoint form of the three-index transition law follows by transposing the actual restriction-form transition composition and the normalized adjunction compositor. Iterated K-flat change of rings is unnecessary.

source.place: Tags 03D7 and 03EK; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS, 06YY and 07A6; derived.tex Tag 015F

proof.text: The strict transition square commutes on sections. Localize it and use the evaluation, scalar and restriction factorization isomorphisms to obtain its derived square; equality is detected after precomposition with localization. Transpose that square through the recorded scalar adjunctions to obtain the displayed transport of adjoint transitions. The recorded derived transition unit gives equal-index adjoint units. The transport square conjugates each adjoint transition by isomorphisms and an equivalence, hence preserves and reflects invertibility, level by level. No inverse limit of a system is used.
